text:
Sarah Li: Heads up — ran a quick fuzz against the org-switch flow and reproduced an authz bypass. Can switch into other orgs if you race the invite acceptance + switch call :warning:
Rahul Mehta: Oof. Can you drop repro steps?
Sarah Li: Yes — quick steps:
```
# create invite for target org (invite_id)
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer userA' /api/orgs/123/invites -d '{"email":"alt@example.com"}'
# from another session, trigger org switch at same time
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer userA' /api/orgs/switch -d '{"org_id":123}'
# race window: accept invite + switch within ~150-300ms
```
Result: switch returns 200 and subsequent requests are scoped to org 123 even though user membership wasn't fully reconciled yet.
Eva Gomez: I can see anomalous org_id writes in the audit stream around 2026-03-19T22:15:xx. @secops-bot can you pull full session traces and any elevated tokens from 22:00-23:00 UTC?
secops-bot: Search started for traces 2026-03-19T22:00Z..2026-03-19T23:00Z (query id q_180300). Will post results when ready.
Kenji Sato: Containment plan: 1) flip feature flag for org-switch off (canary), 2) rollback the last deploy that touched org reconciliation, 3) bulk revoke sessions for suspected accounts. I'll push the flag now.
Rahul Mehta: Quick Q: do we need to rotate any long-lived service tokens or KMS keys used by org-linker? My initial take: no KMS rotation yet — this is logic-level authz bug, but we should check any service tokens used for cross-service calls.
Sarah Li: Patch incoming — adding strict membership verification server-side (lookup user->org membership in single DB transaction) + DB-level constraint to prevent transient writes without confirmed membership. Also adding an explicit audit event type `org_switch_attempt` with origin IP, session id, and token id.
Eva Gomez: I'll draft comms for Product/Legal. We should include timeline + impacted orgs (so far we see 3 org IDs with suspicious writes).
Kenji Sato: Flag flipped off at 1803001250, rollback started 1803001270. I've revoked sessions for 6 accounts that matched the traces. Also rate-limiting the switch endpoint until patch deploys. Next steps: add mutex per-user for switch flow to eliminate race.
secops-bot: Search complete (q_180300): 12 sessions matched, 3 distinct impacted orgs. Creating incident ticket INC-2026-045 and attaching traces.
Rahul Mehta: Assigning follow-ups: Kenji -> containment/rollback (done), Sarah -> patch + unit/integration tests, Eva -> comms + compliance notification, Rahul -> audit schema + replay logs for detection rules. ETA 4h for patch + rollout. :thumbsup:
Sarah Li: I'll open a PR with tests and a migration for the FK constraint. Will tag sec-review.
Kenji Sato: Good work catching this. Postmortem to include: timeline of requests, root cause (race on membership reconciliation), remediation (DB constraint + mutex + feature-flag gating), detection (new audit event + SIEM rule), and customer outreach plan.
Eva Gomez: Notifying CISO + Incident Response channel now. We'll sync at 1803001350 for status update.
Rahul Mehta: Also adding a short-term SIEM rule to alert on org_switch_attempt where user org mapping doesn't match immediate DB state.
Sarah Li: Patch linked in PR #3245. Running canary tests now.
